name: the opt-in gate never stops the script
why: springsteenlyrics.com support is opt-in (sa_enable_springsteenlyrics, default off). Without the gate a published MusicBrainz script would rewrite another site's page for every user who has it installed.

name: no <h1> is injected for the toolbar
why: The SL list pages have no <h1>/<h2>; without the injected anchor init stops at its required-elements check and no button is offered at all.

name: fetched pages are not converted
why: Page 1 is the live document, converted at click time; page 2 arrives as raw cards. Skipping the conversion there drops every fetched page's rows, and the row count is what notices.

name: Load from Disk does not convert the fresh page's cards
why: After a reload the live page holds cards again. Without the disk-path conversion the headers block fabricates a bare table shell at the end of <body>, outside the site's content block.
grep: a reopened list renders in place

name: the navigation guard compares the path only
why: Every SL page is one PHP script told apart by its query string, so a path-only comparison calls collection.php?item=… the same page as the list and lets an item link discard the loaded table without asking.
grep: following an item link from the table asks first

name: Duration is not declared a ':'-aligned integer column
why: The integerColumns align ':' entry is what makes _sortColumnKind() sort Duration as a duration. As text, the 73-minute "1:13:36" sorts before "31:09.55" and the unknown "?:??" is not pinned last.

name: the site's "–" duration is kept verbatim
why: The ':'-aligned column split-aligns every cell, and a colon-less "–" renders as ":–". The converter writes MusicBrainz's "?:??" placeholder instead.
grep: card fields and flags are parsed

name: a card without a copies line is not counted as one copy
why: "I have N copies" only appears for N >= 2; the site's own "Nb. of copies = 1" filter shows that no line means one copy. A blank cell would also sort and filter apart from the 1s.
grep: card fields are parsed into their own columns

name: the trailing-parenthesis split takes the FIRST group
why: "Label (Cat #)" and "Release date (Original year)" end in one parenthesised group, but a label may carry its own parentheses; only the LAST group is the catalogue number or year.

name: First date ignores a day range
why: "16-17 Sep 1967" must start on the 16th; without the range group the regex anchors on "17 Sep".

name: the detection loop ignores the host
why: Recorded honestly as a guard no spec can see today: no MusicBrainz matcher claims /collection.php or /bootlegs.php, and no MusicBrainz URL reaches the SL matchers, so detection gives the same answer without it. It exists for the NEXT broad MusicBrainz matcher (several are bare path.includes() checks).
